utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Morning, everyone. Can you hear me over that noise? Someone's got their mic open on the floor.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah, got you. I'm hiding in the canteen, staring at the broken coffee machine. Again.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: You've got the charity bake sale on Friday, though. Today. Cake instead of coffee.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: That's not a substitute, Callum. That's a separate requirement.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, before we get into nutritional engineering—Friday 30 October. Let's do the finished bits first.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah so, tested the CT1 yesterday and it's all fine now.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: That's the one that was giving you grief?

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: That's it. Finished, nothing carried over from that.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And I tested the air compressor yesterday and it's all fine now. That one's closed as well.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Lovely. Makes a change hearing a list of things that work.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: One more for that list: already swapped the filter on the boiler yesterday. Done, not another job for today.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Cheers. Useful to separate those out.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Just an observation from me—I saw the pressure on the Main Water Isolation Valve dip for a few minutes. It came back on its own.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: So it recovered without anyone touching anything?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah. Just passing on what I saw, not raising a job from it.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Similar sort of thing: noticed the Gas Turbine 2 was running a bit warm on nights but it settled down.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Right, settled rather than still climbing. Got you.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Exactly. Observation only, no new action there.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Less good news, we're still waiting on parts for the CV01. Nothing we can do until they arrive.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Nothing on the repair, you mean? We've still got the near miss hanging over us.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, the physical repair. That's blocked on parts. Different thing from the write-up.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: I'll write up the near miss at the CV01. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Right, Sarah Okafor on the near miss write-up, first priority. Not claiming the repair's suddenly available.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Exactly, I'll do the write-up. The parts situation stays as it is.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: And I can't get to the IM1 until production gives us a window.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: There isn't a window available to give you at the moment, no.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: Okay. Still blocked then, not something I'm committing to do today.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: We also need someone to update the risk assessment for work on the booster pump by 11am. Not an emergency but don't let it slip. Any capacity?

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Um, I haven't got the capacity to take that on. Don't put it against me just because it's a risk assessment.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Understood. Anyone else able to own that?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Not me, sorry. I can't promise that one.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right. Nobody taking it, then. It's still needed by 11am, and it's unowned—not quietly allocated to Grace.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Marcus, can you inspect the line one HPU for leaks next week? That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Next week, yeah? Just checking the 'straight away' bit isn't you moving it into this morning.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: No, next week is still the timing. Safety critical, straight away when that work comes up next week, not something to leave sitting.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Understood. I'll inspect the line one HPU for leaks next week, with that safety-critical urgency.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah, that distinction makes sense. Timing and priority aren't the same box.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Marcus, can you also run the monthly fire alarm test next Tuesday? Normal priority for that one.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll run the monthly fire alarm test next Tuesday. Normal priority, got it.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Next Tuesday's the 3rd, just so we're all looking at the same week.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yep. End of October's disappeared on us.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: While we're on dates, I'll send the shift handover report round on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Fiona. The shift handover report, on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yep, I'll send it round then.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: We've still got the jam on the palletiser, too. That's the other production hold-up.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: I'll clear the jam and check the sensors on the palletiser at half two. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Sorry, talked over the end there—you're taking both the jam and the sensor checks?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Both, yeah. I'll clear the jam and check the sensors on the palletiser. At half two.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Okay, Fiona has both. Half two stays the timing, and it's first priority at that slot because it's holding production up.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the priority from production. Not a 'have a look if you're passing' one.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: On the spares, I'll order spare parts for the big boiler on Friday.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: That's not an emergency order, is it?

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: No, not an emergency but don't let it slip. I'll get the order for the big boiler placed on Friday.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Grace. Friday as in today, yes?

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yes, today. My head's still halfway through Thursday, apparently.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And Grace Liu, can you sort the training records for the new starters today? Low priority.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll sort the training records for the new starters today. Low priority, understood.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: So that's not jumping ahead of the production hold-ups?

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: No, definitely low priority. Still today, but it doesn't jump the queue.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Fine, that's clear. I've got that one.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And the blocked items stay blocked. Mentioning them in the stand-up hasn't magically made parts or a production window appear.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: Sadly not. And the filter I mentioned is finished, so don't drag that back into the open list either.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Same for CT1. Yesterday's good news is allowed to stay good news.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Unlike the coffee machine. That's just become part of the furniture now.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Cake, I'm telling you. Much less disappointing.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, thanks all. We've been clear about what's taken and what isn't. Let's leave it there.
